As forestry investors chased carbon credits, grazing land prices rose 9.7%, according to Real Estate Institute of New Zealand data. Digby Thompson, a manager on Ramsden's farm, drives an ATV down a slope of pasture. REUTERS/Hollie Adams Sheep wait to be shorn in a barn in central Hawke’s Bay. REUTERS/Hollie Adams Dairy land, because it’s generally more expensive, has largely escaped forestry conversion and seen price rises of just 3.7%. Foreign investors have acquired more than 1,000 square kilometers of farmland for conversion to forestry since 2017, according to data from the government’s Overseas Investment Office. Ingka Investments, the investment arm of the company that operates most IKEA stores worldwide, owns 430 square kilometers of forest in New Zealand, some of which is in the ETS. Ingka says its rationale is long-term timber, not carbon-credit income. “The heart of our core investment is more in the timber,” said Dylan Foster, forestland operations manager at Ingka Investments. Dylan Foster, forestland operations manager at Ingka Investments, the investment arm of the company that operates most IKEA stores worldwide, inspects a company forests near Porangahau. REUTERS/Hollie Adams Ingka says it is investing in carbon forests for long-term timber, not just carbon-credit income. REUTERS/Hollie Adams Pine forest borders Alex Renner's sheep and beef farm near Pongaroa. REUTERS/Hollie Adams CHEAP CREDITS, HARDER EMISSIONS CUTS Supporters of the ETS say forestry is essential to reaching New Zealand’s climate targets. Climate Change Minister Simon Watts called it a “cost-effective way” to reduce net emissions, because of the country’s established forestry sector and favorable growing conditions. The Climate Change Commission , an independent advisory body, expects ETS forests to deliver a quarter of the emissions reductions needed for New Zealand’s 2026-2030 target, and nearly half of those needed for its 2031-2035 target. But critics say the scheme relies too heavily on offsets, rather than direct emissions cuts. Because planting and maintaining forests is relatively cheap, they say polluters can buy credits rather than make the costlier investments required to transition to cleaner fuels or technology.

A newly planted Ingka forest near the town of Waipukurau. REUTERS/Cordelia Hsu

Climate Change Commission chief executive Jo Hendy said the ETS is essentially “functioning as an offsetting scheme.” The government says New Zealand is on track to meet its near-term climate goals. “Forestry is not the whole plan,” Watts said in response to emailed questions from Reuters. Late last year, the government tightened the ETS rules for non-native species, including pine, on more productive land. Preliminary data released by Beef + Lamb New Zealand last month showed purchases for wholesale conversions had slowed to nearly 160 square kilometers, less than half of the total the year before. However, the industry group said the total could rise once data is finalized. Cattle graze near plantations outside Porangahau, an area that was damaged by wildfires in 2025. REUTERS/Hollie Adams FEWER ANIMALS, FEWER JOBS, THINNER COMMUNITIES For farmer David Buick, high prices for lands suitable for forestry conversion in 2020 offered a chance to trade up to a better farm in the Pongaroa area. “We’ve had to work for every cent we’ve got and so for me it was a good decision to sell that on a forestry high,” he said, while acknowledging the issues of blanket planting of pine trees. But the effects on those left behind ripple beyond the paddock gates. Alex Renner, a sheep and beef farmer who lives about a 10-minute drive from Pongaroa, says he has watched young families leave the area as sheep and beef farms are converted to carbon forestry. REUTERS/Hollie Adams Farmer Alex Renner, who lives a 10-minute drive from Pongaroa, said five neighboring farms had been converted to forestry over the last decade. As more land moved into trees, young families disappeared. The rugby club folded in 2022, after they couldn’t find enough players to field a team. The community-run daycare closed in 2023, in part due to falling enrollment. The population of Owahanga, the rural area that includes Pongaroa, has fallen an estimated 2.6% over the past decade, according to Statistics New Zealand, deepening a decades-long decline driven by reduced demand for rural workers. “We’ve lost a lot of those young families,” Renner said. “It’s people that make a community.” A drone view of Pongaroa, a rural settlement on New Zealand’s North Island about a three-hour drive northeast of Wellington. REUTERS/Hollie Adams Marty Hull, former club captain of the local rugby club in Pongaroa. The club folded in 2022 after it couldn’t find enough players to field a team. REUTERS/Hollie Adams The carbon-credit boom is transforming community life in small towns and villages like Pongaroa. REUTERS/Hollie Adams At a Hawke’s Bay shearing shed, Brandon Coombe-Gray sees the changes one lamb at a time. When farms are planted in pine, fewer ewes mean fewer lambs – and less work for shearers, truck drivers, stock agents and rural contractors. A shearing station that once carried about 10,000 ewes is now planted entirely in pine, he said. “Not one single ewe is there to be seen.” Forestry industry representatives reject the suggestion that the industry hollows out rural regions.The sector provides jobs, supports key industries and generates about NZ$6.5 billion (US$3.7 billion) in annual export earnings, said Elizabeth Heeg, chief executive of the New Zealand Forest Owners Association. Red meat exports generate around NZ$12 billion (US$6.9 billion) in revenue.

Sheep shearer Brandon Coombe-Gray sees the changes one lamb at a time. Fewer ewes mean fewer lambs — and less work for shearers, truck drivers, stock agents and rural contractors, he says.

‘ONE LESS FARM THAT CAN BE BOUGHT’ For some farmers who border forest blocks, downsides include difficulty coordinating with absentee farmers on pest control and damage from goats, deer, pigs and possums moving onto their land. Heeg said that forestry managers “absolutely had active management” of their properties. In 2023, Cyclone Gabrielle – the costliest storm on record in New Zealand – washed forestry debris down waterways in some areas, damaging infrastructure and property. In parts of Hawke’s Bay and Wairarapa, farmers also worry that expanding forest could increase wildfire risks during hot, dry summers. Nateva, one of the largest carbon forest operators in New Zealand, said it runs extensive pest-control and wildfire-prevention programs, removing fire-prone grasses and vegetation from roadsides and tracks. For sheep shearer Axle Reid, the shift to forestry feels like a door closing. The 37-year-old said he had once hoped to save enough from shearing to eventually buy his own place. As more land was converted to forestry and prices rose, he said he felt he’d been pushed out of the market. Watching farmland convert to forestry “feels like a kick in the teeth,” Reid said. “Once they go into forestry, it’s one less farm that can be bought.” Pine trees dot a ridgeline near Porangahau. REUTERS/Hollie Adams

item.title: Agropalma vê alta de 20% na nova safra após El Niño de 2023 afetar ciclo passado
item.description: A Agropalma, líder na fabricação de óleo de palma do Brasil, projeta um aumento de cerca de 20% na produção da safra que se inicia em relação à anterior, após ter sido atingida no ano passado pelos efeitos do El Niño de 2023 e 2024, disse um diretor da companhia à Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Roberto Samora
item.content:encoded: A Agropalma, líder na fabricação de óleo de palma do Brasil, projeta um aumento de cerca de 20% na produção da safra que se inicia em relação à anterior, após ter sido atingida no ano passado pelos efeitos do El Niño de 2023 e 2024, disse um diretor da companhia à Reuters. A palma, cultivada na Amazônia brasileira, leva duas safras para refletir mais fortemente os efeitos das altas temperaturas e redução de chuvas decorrentes do fenômeno climático, o que explica o aumento esperado para 2026, ainda que este seja um ano de El Niño. A situação sinaliza ainda que o fenômeno climático de 2026/27, que pode ser um dos mais fortes da história, poderia impactar a produção nos próximos anos da empresa e de outros operadores do setor, concentrado no Pará -- o Norte do país geralmente enfrenta tempo mais seco e quente em anos de El Niño. "Enquanto a maior parte do mundo usa o termo 'climate change', a gente aqui prefere 'climate disorder'... para nós aqui, o que está acontecendo que é muito visível: é uma modificação em todo o regime climático, não só de chuvas, como de temperatura", disse o diretor Agrícola da Agropalma, André Borba. Embora seja uma potência agrícola e grande parte do país esteja localizada na faixa tropical do planeta, o Brasil é um importador de óleo de palma, já que grande parte de sua produção de óleo vegetal vem da soja. Oscilações na oferta brasileira, que normalmente gira em torno de 600 mil toneladas de óleo de palma por ano, poderiam impactar as importações, estimadas em [USN:L1N43N15V TEXT:"cerca de 30%"] do consumo anual de 1 milhão de toneladas. A última boa safra da Agropalma, que responde por um quarto da produção nacional, foi a de 2022, disse Borba, citando impactos de El Niños passados. Ele explicou que o cacho de frutos da palma colhido em 2026 é formado dois anos antes. "Então, se nós temos um estresse hídrico, estresse de temperatura ou de umidade, ao invés de a palmeira produzir uma inflorescência feminina que vai virar o cacho, ela produz uma masculina que não vira produção." "No ano de 2024, nós tivemos bastante problema com falta de chuva e com aumento de temperatura, que de certa maneira estão prejudicando este ano. Mas o ano de 2025 sofreu mais ainda por conta do ano de 2023", ressaltou. Apesar de o clima ter desafiado a produção nos últimos anos, o Brasil tem potencial para mais do que triplicar o plantio de palma de óleo em um período de dez anos, utilizando áreas desmatadas anteriormente na Amazônia, com impulso da demanda por matérias-primas para a produção de biocombustíveis avançados como o SAF de aviação, afirmou o presidente da Associação Brasileira de Produtores de Óleo de Palma (Abrapalma), Victor Almeida, em entrevista recente à Reuters. Borba preferiu não comentar sobre planos de expansão da Agropalma, adquirida este ano pelo grupo [USN:L1N3ZS1EI TEXT:"colombiano Daabon"], que passou a ter uma fatia majoritária na empresa. No processo produtivo, a companhia usa 75% de frutos de produção própria, comprando o restante de terceiros, incluindo agricultores familiares. NOVA SAFRA A Agropalma está perto de iniciar a colheita nos meses que registram maiores produtividades. Os maiores volumes de colheita de frutos são em outubro, com cerca de 12% da produção no ano, novembro, com 15%, e dezembro, com 10%, disse o diretor Agrícola da Agropalma. Em abril, normalmente são os menores volumes, próximos de 4%. "É uma planta que depende bastante do clima. Ela não produz em áreas com temperaturas baixas e tampouco produz em áreas com pouca chuva. Então, ela demanda mais ou menos 150 milímetros de chuva por mês... essa é a razão de nós estarmos aqui na região Norte, mais próximo da linha do Equador, que é uma das regiões que mais chove no Brasil...", explicou. Sob a influência do El Niño, contudo, ele disse acreditar que as temperaturas mais altas terão maior influência na safra do que a escassez de chuvas. "A temperatura média este ano está mais ou menos 29 graus (Celsius), dois graus acima do normal. As máximas, que geralmente chegam a 32 graus, este ano estão chegando a 36." Ele disse ter expectativa de que o El Niño afete a lavoura até fevereiro do próximo ano, já que o fenômeno deverá adiar as chuvas que normalmente voltam a se intensificar na região em dezembro, estendendo-se até junho. Para lidar com o problema, Borba destacou que a companhia adota a puerária, uma leguminosa, como cobertura verde, o que reduz a temperatura do solo de 54 graus para 23. "Com essa temperatura bem menor, nós conseguimos manter mais umidade no solo e nosso plantio sofre menos com os efeitos da falta de chuva e da temperatura." A puerária tem ainda a capacidade de captar o nitrogênio da atmosfera, fixando-o no solo, o que permite redução de custos com adubação. Além disso, a leguminosa atrai insetos predadores de pragas, dispensando o uso de pesticidas químicos.

item.title: BID elabora plano de dois anos para a Venezuela e diz que setor elétrico e áreas sociais são fundamentais
item.description: O Banco Interamericano de Desenvolvimento está elaborando um plano de atuação de dois anos para a Venezuela, com foco parcial nos setores de energia elétrica e proteção social, afirmou nesta segunda-feira o presidente do BID, Ilan Goldfajn.
item.dc:creator: Rodrigo Campos
item.content:encoded: O Banco Interamericano de Desenvolvimento está elaborando um plano de atuação de dois anos para a Venezuela, com foco parcial nos setores de energia elétrica e proteção social, afirmou nesta segunda-feira o presidente do BID, Ilan Goldfajn. “Estamos, é claro, retomando nosso envolvimento”, disse Goldfajn em entrevista à Reuters. “Temos missões na Venezuela para analisar a situação, lidar com o quadro macroeconômico, examinar os dados e elaborar uma nota de compromisso — um documento no qual possamos definir o que planejamos fazer nos próximos dois anos.” O BID é a maior instituição financeira de desenvolvimento da América Latina e do Caribe e conta com 48 países-membros, incluindo 26 membros mutuários na região. O banco suspendeu a concessão de novos empréstimos à Venezuela em maio de 2018, após o país ter atrasado pagamentos, e ainda possui cerca de US$2 bilhões em empréstimos venezuelanos pendentes. Goldfajn não informou como os atrasos da Venezuela serão resolvidos nem quando o financiamento poderá ser retomado. “Ainda estamos na fase de planejamento e trabalho com os venezuelanos, mantendo contato e visitando as missões, para ver como podemos trabalhar com eles”, disse ele. Questionado se o BID está preparando sua própria análise de sustentabilidade da dívida para a Venezuela, Goldfajn disse que, em vez disso, o banco estava se concentrando no quadro macroeconômico do país e nas necessidades de cada setor.

item.title: Jarvis Cocker recuerda los comienzos de Pulp en un nuevo documental
item.description: Casi medio siglo después de su formación, Pulp, los ídolos del pop británico, son los protagonistas de un documental que se adentra en las raíces de la banda y en los sueños de infancia de su desgarbado líder, Jarvis Cocker.
item.dc:creator: Shaurya Thapa
item.content:encoded: Casi medio siglo después de su formación, Pulp, los ídolos del pop británico, son los protagonistas de un documental que se adentra en las raíces de la banda y en los sueños de infancia de su desgarbado líder, Jarvis Cocker. En "Pulp: What Do You Do For An Encore?", Cocker narra una serie de recuerdos basados en las entradas de un diario que garabateaba en el colegio, en la ciudad de Sheffield, al norte de Inglaterra, en la década de de 1970, en las que trazaba su "plan maestro" para el éxito de Pulp. "Tenía unos 12 ó 13 años (…) Aún no sabía tocar la guitarra, pero sí sabía escribir", explicó Cocker a Reuters. "Era la realización de un deseo. Supongo que algo así como una manifestación". Convenció a sus amigos para que ensayaran en casa de su madre, sobornándolos con "un poco de cerveza rubia". La película, dirigida por Garth Jennings, director de "Son of Rambow", pasa a abordar su etapa de estudios de cine y bellas artes en Londres, en el St Martin’s College, inmortalizado en su futuro éxito "Common People". "Me licencié, pero (…) lo que realmente me atraía era componer canciones", añadió. "Creo que ésa es mi forma de intentar darle sentido al mundo y a mí mismo". Pulp tuvo dificultades para alcanzar el éxito en la década de 1980, pero luego se abrió paso en el gran público en la de 1990 con álbumes como "His 'N' Hers" y "Different Class" —ganador del Premio Mercury—, además de una serie de éxitos que van desde "Do You Remember The First Time?" hasta "Disco 2000" y "Help the Aged". Tras una pausa discográfica de 24 años, regresaron en 2025 con "More", nominado al Premio Mercury. La película recoge las actuaciones de la banda durante sus conciertos de reencuentro en el O2 Arena de Londres. En cuanto al futuro, "creo que no estaré vivo (…) dentro de 24 años, o si lo estoy, no estaré en condiciones", dijo Cocker. "Pero hicimos un álbum. Salió bien (…) Todos seguimos en contacto, así que realmente espero que hagamos algo más. Pero no sé cuánto tiempo llevará". "Pulp: What Do You Do For An Encore?" se estrena en MUBI el 25 de septiembre.

item.title: IDB drafts two-year Venezuela plan, says electricity and social needs are key
item.description: The Inter-American Development Bank is drawing up a two-year engagement plan for Venezuela focused partly on electricity and social protection, IDB President Ilan Goldfajn said on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Rodrigo Campos
item.content:encoded: The Inter-American Development Bank is drawing up a two-year engagement plan for Venezuela focused partly on electricity and social protection, IDB President Ilan Goldfajn said on Monday. “We are, of course, reengaging,” Goldfajn told Reuters in an interview. “We have missions to Venezuela, looking at the situation, dealing with the macroeconomic framework, looking at the data and devising an engagement note, a document where we can say this is what we plan to do in the next two years.” The IDB is the largest development lender in Latin America and the Caribbean and has 48 member countries, including 26 borrowing members in the region. It stopped making new loans to Venezuela in May 2018 after the country fell behind on payments, and still has about $2 billion in outstanding Venezuelan loans. Goldfajn did not say how Venezuela’s arrears would be addressed or when financing could resume. “We are still in the moment of planning and working with Venezuelans, engaging and going to the missions, and seeing how we can work with them,” he said. Asked whether the IDB was preparing its own debt-sustainability analysis for Venezuela, Goldfajn said it was instead concentrating on the country’s macroeconomic framework and requirements across individual sectors.

item.title: Índice STOXX 600 sobe com impulso de setores de tecnologia e bancário, enquanto petróleo recua
item.description: Uma recuperação nos papéis dos grandes bancos e das empresas de tecnologia impulsionou as ações europeias nesta segunda-feira, enquanto os preços do petróleo caíram pela quarta sessão consecutiva, fortalecendo o apetite pelo risco no mercado.
item.dc:creator: Sudeshna Ghoshal, Purvi Agarwal
item.content:encoded: Uma recuperação nos papéis dos grandes bancos e das empresas de tecnologia impulsionou as ações europeias nesta segunda-feira, enquanto os preços do petróleo caíram pela quarta sessão consecutiva, fortalecendo o apetite pelo risco no mercado. O índice pan-europeu STOXX 600 (.STOXX) fechou com alta de 1%, registrando seu maior salto diário desde 2 de julho. A maioria das bolsas regionais também encerrou o dia em alta. O movimento marca um início positivo para a semana, com investidores avaliando se a retração do petróleo bruto pode amenizar as pressões inflacionárias. O Banco Central Europeu elevou as taxas de juros no início deste mês para combater a inflação, à medida que a forte dependência das importações de combustível deixa as economias regionais expostas às oscilações nos preços do petróleo. As ações de bancos (.SX7P) estavam entre as que mais valorizaram, com alta de 1,7%. O Société Générale (SOGN.PA) subiu 1,7% e o Banco BPM (BAMI.MI) registrou alta de 4,3%, com este último subindo após especulações da mídia de que o UniCredit (CRDI.MI) e o Crédit Agricole (CAGR.PA) estariam avaliando uma ação conjunta em relação ao banco italiano. As ações do setor de tecnologia (.SX8P) avançaram 1,7%, à medida que o renovado interesse pela inteligência artificial impulsionou ações ligadas ao setor de chips, como a Soitec (SOIT.PA) e a Aixtron (AIXGn.DE) . No entanto, as ações do setor de energia (.SXEP) recuaram 0,8%, conforme os futuros do petróleo Brent caminhavam para sua maior sequência de perdas diárias desde junho, após relatos sugerirem que um volume de oferta acima do esperado estava saindo do Golfo, apesar do conflito em curso com o Irã. O DAX (.GDAXI) da Alemanha subiu 1,1%, com investidores assimilando os resultados das eleições estaduais no nordeste da Alemanha, onde as projeções indicavam que o partido de extrema direita Alternativa para a Alemanha emergia como o maior partido. A Novo Nordisk (NOVOb.CO) foi a maior perdedora no STOXX 600, com uma queda de 7,7%, com seus executivos enfrentando perguntas difíceis sobre o poder de fixação de preços da farmacêutica e sua estratégia de negociações, diante do vencimento iminente de patentes, durante o “Capital Markets Day” da empresa. As ações da empresa de biotecnologia Ipsen (IPN.PA) caíram mais de 5% depois que a Agência de Alimentos e Medicamentos dos Estados Unidos (FDA, na sigla inglês) aprovou a versão genérica da Amneal do medicamento de grande sucesso da empresa, o Somatuline. O índice pan-europeu STOXX 600 (.STOXX) fechou em alta de 1,02%, a 641,93 pontos. Em LONDRES, o índice Financial Times (.FTSE) avançou 0,75%, a 10.739,01 pontos. Em FRANKFURT, o índice DAX (.GDAXI) subiu 1,07%, a 25.575,01 pontos. Em PARIS, o índice CAC-40 (.FCHI) ganhou 0,92%, a 8.138,94 pontos. Em MILÃO, o índice Ftse/Mib (.FTMIB) teve valorização de 1,60%, a 52.371,54 pontos. Em MADRI, o índice Ibex-35 (.IBEX) registrou alta de 1,08%, a 19.724,40 pontos. Em LISBOA, o índice PSI20 (.PSI20) valorizou-se 0,79%, a 9.617,39 pontos.

item.title: OpenAI insta a EEUU a liderar los esfuerzos mundiales para desarrollar normas técnicas
item.description: El gigante de la inteligencia artificial OpenAI pidió el lunes que Estados Unidos lidere una iniciativa internacional para desarrollar normas técnicas globales para el sector, incluida la "automejora recursiva", que permite a los sistemas mejorar de forma autónoma sus propias capacidades.
item.dc:creator: Michelle Nichols
item.content:encoded: El gigante de la inteligencia artificial OpenAI pidió el lunes que Estados Unidos lidere una iniciativa internacional para desarrollar normas técnicas globales para el sector, incluida la "automejora recursiva", que permite a los sistemas mejorar de forma autónoma sus propias capacidades. La IA será un asunto clave de debate en la Asamblea General de las Naciones Unidas de esta semana, después de que varios líderes del sector, entre ellos el presidente ejecutivo de OpenAI, Sam Altman, pidieran una ralentización coordinada del desarrollo de esta tecnología cada vez más potente, advirtiendo de que pronto podría mejorar por sí misma y escapar al control humano. En una entrada de blog publicada mientras los líderes mundiales se reúnen en la ONU, OpenAI dijo que es esencial desarrollar un mecanismo que facilite la creación de normas nacionales e internacionales complementarias en materia de IA, junto con métricas comunes y protocolos de notificación de incidentes para una mejor acción colectiva. "Tomar la iniciativa ahora determinará si Estados Unidos da forma al marco global de la IA o si se limita a observar cómo se afianza a su alrededor un sistema fragmentado, desigual y plagado de conflictos. Esto también determinará si la IA avanzada refuerza las redes que ya tienen Estados Unidos y sus aliados; no asumir el liderazgo podría debilitarlas", señaló. Dadas las preocupaciones sobre el daño que la IA podría causar a los seres humanos en el futuro, el sector ha estado debatiendo la posibilidad de ralentizar de forma intencionada el desarrollo. "Modular el desarrollo de la IA no consiste en mantener una velocidad predeterminada. Técnicamente, se trata de garantizar que la investigación sobre la alineación y la aplicación de dicha investigación se mantengan por delante de las capacidades", afirmó OpenAI. La alineación garantiza que la IA actúe de acuerdo con los valores humanos. Altman tiene previsto informar este miércoles a los 15 miembros del Consejo de Seguridad de la ONU sobre la IA y la seguridad internacional. La reunión fue convocada por Francia, que ocupa la presidencia del órgano durante septiembre, y estará presidida por el ministro francés de Europa y Relaciones Exteriores, Jean-Noël Barrot. El Consejo de Seguridad de la ONU, encargado de mantener la paz y la seguridad internacionales, se reunió por primera vez para tratar los riesgos de la IA en 2023, cuando China afirmó que la tecnología no debía convertirse en un "caballo desbocado" y Estados Unidos advirtió contra su uso para censurar o reprimir a la población.

item.title: Lula dice que Brasil usará excedente de cuota de exportación de carne de vacuno de Uruguay a China
item.description: El presidente brasileño, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, dijo el lunes que Uruguay autorizó a Brasil a utilizar el excedente de su cuota de exportación de carne de vacuno a China.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El presidente brasileño, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, dijo el lunes que Uruguay autorizó a Brasil a utilizar el excedente de su cuota de exportación de carne de vacuno a China. "Expresé mi agradecimiento por la autorización concedida a Brasil para utilizar el excedente de la cuota de exportación de carne de vacuno de Uruguay a China", escribió Lula en la red social X tras reunirse con su homólogo uruguayo, Yamandú Orsi, en Nueva York. El Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores de Uruguay no respondió de inmediato a una solicitud de comentarios. En enero, China impuso un arancel adicional del 55% a las importaciones de carne de vacuno que superaran los niveles de cuota de los principales proveedores, entre ellos Brasil, en una medida destinada a proteger su industria ganadera nacional. De noviembre a junio, Brasil ya había exportado el 98,5% de su cuota de 1,1 millones de toneladas, según indicó StoneX en un reporte publicado en julio, añadiendo que se agotaría en agosto. Se prevé que el volumen total de exportaciones de carne de vacuno de Brasil caiga un 10% interanual en 2026, según estimó a principios de este año la asociación sectorial Abiec, en un contexto de restricciones impuestas por Pekín y de una reciente limitación de las exportaciones brasileñas de carne a la Unión Europea.

item.title: EEUU suspende vuelos en aeropuertos del este por un corte de fibra óptica en una obra
item.description: La Administración Federal de Aviación (FAA) suspendió el lunes vuelos en concurridos aeropuertos de la costa este de Nueva York, como Filadelfia y Boston, porque un cable de fibra óptica se había cortado accidentalmente en una obra de Nueva Jersey.
item.dc:creator: David Shepardson
item.content:encoded: La Administración Federal de Aviación (FAA) suspendió el lunes vuelos en concurridos aeropuertos de la costa este de Nueva York, como Filadelfia y Boston, porque un cable de fibra óptica se había cortado accidentalmente en una obra de Nueva Jersey. Se ordenaron paradas en tierra en los aeropuertos John F. Kennedy y LaGuardia, así como en el de Teterboro en Nueva Jersey, justo cuando 130 líderes mundiales y decenas de ministros llegaban a Nueva York para la reunión anual de alto nivel de la Asamblea General de las Naciones Unidas. El administrador de la FAA, Bryan Bedford, explicó a periodistas que una línea de fibra óptica de reserva había sido cortada accidentalmente por un equipo de obras en Nueva Jersey, lo que provocó importantes restricciones en los vuelos. Bedford dijo que un nuevo circuito estaría operativo en breve. No estaba claro cuándo se levantarían las suspensiones de despegues en los aeropuertos del área de Nueva York. FlightAware, una web de seguimiento de vuelos, indicó que más de 600 vuelos en Newark y Filadelfia, más del 20%, habían sufrido retrasos en el Centro de Control de Aproximación por Radar de Filadelfia. Newark es un importante centro de operaciones de United Airlines (UAL.O) , mientras que Filadelfia lo es de American Airlines (AAL.O) . El problema también obligó a desviar varios vuelos a otros aeropuertos. Flightradar24, un sitio web de seguimiento de vuelos, indicó que las operaciones sufrían retrasos de 112 minutos en promedio en Newark. En mayo de 2025, la instalación que controla el tráfico aéreo que entra y sale del aeropuerto de Newark sufrió una serie de importantes cortes en las comunicaciones. La FAA señaló el año pasado que una interrupción de las telecomunicaciones afectó a las comunicaciones y a las pantallas de radar del TRACON de Filadelfia. El año pasado, el Congreso aprobó 12.500 millones de dólares para abordar el envejecimiento del sistema de control del tráfico aéreo e impulsar la contratación de controladores, tras décadas de quejas por la congestión aeroportuaria y los retrasos en los vuelos, así como una serie de problemas tecnológicos en los últimos años.

item.title: Venezuelan delegation led by Rodriguez to discuss debt, energy in US, sources say
item.description: A Venezuelan delegation led by interim President Delcy Rodriguez taking part in the United Nations General Assembly this week plans to discuss energy, debt and mining issues with counterparties in the US, two sources close to the preparations said.
item.dc:creator: Marianna Parraga, Vivian Sequera
item.content:encoded: A Venezuelan delegation led by interim President Delcy Rodriguez taking part in the United Nations General Assembly this week plans to discuss energy, debt and mining issues with counterparties in the US, two sources close to the preparations said. The talks are expected to lead to the signing of agreements as part of US President Donald Trump's plans to rebuild the South American country's key industries, according to the sources. Rodriguez arrived in New York early on Monday with her team. It was her first trip to the US after taking office as Venezuela's interim president in January under Washington's oversight, following the capture of then President Nicolas Maduro by US forces. The top US diplomat in Venezuela, John Barrett, received her at the airport, Venezuela's state TV said. Venezuelan ministers and top officials have been advancing in negotiations for months ahead of Rodriguez's trip to New York, where she is scheduled to meet Trump on Tuesday. On Monday, Rodriguez was scheduled to meet with UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres, according to his agenda. The planned meeting between Trump and Rodriguez — who was Venezuela's vice president under Maduro — will take place on the sidelines of a reception hosted by the US President, the US Ambassador to the United Nations, Mike Waltz, said during a recent press briefing call. Venezuela's Foreign Affairs and Information ministries did not immediately reply to requests for comment. Some Venezuela-owned buildings in New York, including a consulate and the office of the country's UN mission, have recently been renovated, according to media reports. Oil Minister Paula Henao, Mining Minister Hector Silva and top officials from state oil company PDVSA participated this month in a G20 energy conference in Houston, where [USN:S0N42Y01V TEXT:"a memorandum of understanding"] was inked with US oil producer Continental Resources for an area in Venezuela's main output region, the Orinoco Belt. A separate contract was also signed granting US investment firm Heeney Capital operational and export rights for a gold mine. Another [USN:L6N458178 TEXT:"preliminary agreement"] has been in negotiation for months with US energy major ExxonMobil , which could ultimately lead to its return to Venezuela's oilfields, sources said this month. For its part, the Inter-American Development Bank is drawing up a two-year engagement plan for Venezuela focused partly on electricity and social protection, its President Ilan Goldfajn told Reuters on Monday. The effort includes missions to examine the nation's macroeconomic framework and data and to estimate investment needs across different sectors.

item.title: Reino Unido acusa homem por supostos crimes relacionados ao genocídio em Ruanda
item.description: Um ruandês de 65 anos foi acusado de crimes relacionados ao genocídio, supostamente cometidos durante o massacre dos tutsis em Ruanda, em 1994, informaram promotores britânicos nesta segunda-feira.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Um ruandês de 65 anos foi acusado de crimes relacionados ao genocídio, supostamente cometidos durante o massacre dos tutsis em Ruanda, em 1994, informaram promotores britânicos nesta segunda-feira. Vincent Brown, anteriormente conhecido como Vincent Bajinya, foi acusado de um crime de participação em genocídio e de seis crimes de participação em assassinatos classificados como crimes contra a humanidade. A Equipe de Crimes de Guerra da Polícia Antiterrorismo do Reino Unido informou que Brown foi acusado de incentivar outras pessoas a matar tutsis em Kigali, em abril de 1994. A investigação teve início em 2019, após um pedido do governo ruandês, e envolveu anos de cooperação internacional, acrescentou a equipe. Brown foi acusado de ter “dirigido e incitado atos de homicídio e genocídio cometidos por terceiros”, informou a Procuradoria da Coroa (CPS, na sigla em inglês). As acusações contra Brown foram as primeiras apresentadas no Reino Unido relacionadas ao genocídio ruandês, acrescentou a CPS. Brown, que se encontra em prisão preventiva, deve comparecer à Corte de Magistrados de Westminster, em Londres, na terça-feira. A polícia informou que as investigações sobre outras seis pessoas continuam em andamento, incluindo dois homens presos em 2024 e 2026 sob suspeita de genocídio e crimes contra a humanidade, que permanecem em liberdade condicional. Mais de 800 mil tutsis e hutus moderados foram mortos em 100 dias durante o genocídio de 1994, orquestrado pela maioria hutu no poder e meticulosamente executado por autoridades locais e cidadãos comuns.

item.title: Brazil to use Uruguay's surplus of beef export quota to China, Lula says
item.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva said on Monday that Uruguay had authorized Brazil to use the surplus from its beef export quota to China.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva said on Monday that Uruguay had authorized Brazil to use the surplus from its beef export quota to China. "I expressed my gratitude for the authorization granted to Brazil to use the surplus from Uruguay's beef export quota to China," Lula wrote on X after meeting with his Uruguayan counterpart, Yamandu Orsi, in New York. Uruguay's foreign ministry did not immediately reply to a request for comment. China [USN:L1N3Y1040 TEXT:"in January "][USN:L1N3Y1040 TEXT:"imposed"] an added 55% tariff on beef imports that exceed quota levels from key suppliers, including Brazil, in a move to protect its domestic cattle industry. From November to June, Brazil had [USN:L1N4380RN TEXT:"already shipped"] 98.5% of its 1.1 million metric ton quota, StoneX said in a report in July, adding the quota would be filled by August. Brazil's total beef export volumes are expected to drop 10% year-on-year in 2026, industry group Abiec estimated earlier this year, amid restrictions imposed by Beijing and a recent curb on Brazilian meat exports to the European Union.

item.title: OpenAI calls for US to take lead in global efforts to develop technical standards
item.description: Artificial intelligence giant OpenAI called on Monday for the United States to lead an international effort to develop global technical standards for frontier AI, including recursive self-improvement, where systems can autonomously enhance their own capabilities.
item.dc:creator: Michelle Nichols
item.content:encoded: Artificial intelligence giant OpenAI called on Monday for the United States to lead an international effort to develop global technical standards for frontier AI , including recursive self-improvement, where systems can autonomously enhance their own capabilities. AI will be a key topic of discussion at the high-level UN General Assembly this week after several AI industry leaders — including OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman — called for a coordinated slowdown of the development of the [USN:L6N45A0PY TEXT:"increasingly powerful technology"], warning it could soon improve on its own and slip beyond human control. In a blog post published as world leaders gather at the United Nations, OpenAI said it was essential that a mechanism to facilitate complementary national and international frontier standards be developed, along with common measurements and incident reporting protocols for better collective action. "Leading now will determine whether the United States shapes the global AI framework or watches a fragmented, uneven, and conflict-ridden system take hold around it. This will also determine whether advanced AI strengthens the networks that the United States and its allies already have; failing to lead may weaken them," OpenAI wrote in Monday's blog post. Given worries about AI potentially harming humans in the future, the industry has been talking about intentionally slowing development, or "pacing". "Pacing AI development is not about maintaining a predetermined speed. Technically, it is about ensuring that alignment research and deployment of that research stay ahead of capabilities," OpenAI said. Alignment ensures AI acts in line with human values. UN SECURITY COUNCIL TO MEET [USN:L6N45A15J TEXT:"Altman is due to brief"] the 15-member UN Security Council on Wednesday on AI and international security. The meeting has been convened by France, which is the president of the body for September, and will be chaired by French Minister for Europe and Foreign Affairs Jean-Noël Barrot. The UN Security Council, which is charged with maintaining international peace and security, met for the first time on the risks of artificial intelligence in 2023, when China said the technology should not become a "runaway horse" and the United States warned against its use to censor or repress people. US President Donald Trump's administration has rejected calls to slow down AI development, wary that any pause would only hand China room to close the gap in a technology it views as central to national and economic security. Trump said earlier this month that the US already has guardrails in place to regulate AI development, adding that China would benefit from the doubt being cast on AI development. Trump is [USN:L8N45A068 TEXT:"scheduled to meet"] with Chinese President Xi Jinping this week in Washington.

item.title: Jarvis Cocker remembers Pulp's first time in new documentary
item.description: Almost half a century after their birth, Britpop darlings Pulp are stars of a documentary that delves back into the band's roots in the childhood dreams of gangly frontman Jarvis Cocker.
item.dc:creator: Shaurya Thapa
item.content:encoded: Almost half a century after their birth, Britpop darlings Pulp are stars of a documentary that delves back into the band's roots in the childhood dreams of gangly frontman Jarvis Cocker. In "Pulp: What Do You Do For An Encore?" Cocker narrates flashbacks based on diary entries he scrawled out at school in the northern English city of Sheffield in the 1970s, mapping out his "masterplan" for Pulp's success. "I was maybe 12 or 13 ... I couldn't play the guitar yet but I could write," Cocker told Reuters. "It was ... wish fulfilment. I suppose like manifesting." He got his friends to rehearse at his mother's house, bribing them by "buying some lager". The film, directed by "Son of Rambow"'s Garth Jennings, moves on to his time studying film and fine art in London — at the "St Martin's College" immortalised in their future hit "Common People". "I graduated but ... what really I felt a pull to do was to write songs," he added. "I think that's my way of trying to make sense of the world and out of myself." Pulp struggled to find success in the 1980s, then rose to mainstream success in the 1990s with albums such as "His 'N' Hers" and the Mercury Prize-winning "Different Class" and a string of other hits from "Do You Remember The First Time?" to "Disco 2000" to "Help the Aged". After a 24-year-long recording hiatus, they returned in 2025 with the Mercury Prize-nominated "More". The film captures the band’s performances from their reunion shows at London’s O2 Arena. As for the future, "I think I won't be alive ... in 24 years, or if I am, I won't be up to it," Cocker said. "But, we did an album. It went well ... Everybody is still talking to each other, so I would really hope that we will make something else. But I don't know how long that will take." "Pulp: What Do You Do For An Encore?" begins streaming on MUBI on September 25.

item.title: Bears QB Caleb Williams (hamstring) is 'week-to-week'
item.description: Bears quarterback Caleb Williams' hamstring injury is going to be a "week-to-week thing," Chicago coach Ben Johnson said Monday in a radio interview on ESPN 1000.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Bears quarterback Caleb Williams' hamstring injury is going to be a "week-to-week thing," Chicago coach Ben Johnson said Monday in a radio interview on ESPN 1000. The Ringer reported that Williams avoided serious injury in Sunday's 9-3 loss to Minnesota and hadn't yet been ruled out for next Monday's home game against Philadelphia. Johnson, though, seemed to indicate otherwise, without providing a definitive timeline. "It sounds like it's going to be a week-to-week deal for him," Johnson said. "I've got to still talk with our trainer. We'll do that here shortly and I'll have the lowdown from him. But it sounds like it's week-to-week but will likely miss some time." Williams was hurt when attempting to reach the end zone with a fourth-quarter scramble on the wet turf at Soldier Field. He awkwardly tumbled to the turf on his knees and rolled over a couple times in pain before the Bears' medical staff attended to him. He was transported to the locker room on a cart and had a towel over his head before removing it and pumping his arm into the air multiple times to rev up the Chicago fans. The initial reporting on Sunday said that Williams sustained a Grade 1 hamstring strain. Williams, 24, has made 36 consecutive starts since the Bears drafted him No. 1 overall in 2024. He has completed 65.5% of his passes for 407 yards, two touchdowns and one interception this season for Chicago (1-1). If Williams is unable to go Monday against the Eagles (2-0), it would mark the first time Johnson has been forced to start a backup quarterback as an offensive play-caller. Jared Goff started all 51 games for the Lions from 2022-24, when Johnson was Detroit's offensive coordinator. Backup Tyson Bagent completed 5 of 9 passes for 54 yards in relief on Sunday. He has thrown for 971 yards, three TDs and six interceptions in 13 games (four starts) over the last four seasons. All four of his starts came as a rookie in 2023 for Chicago. If Bagent, 26, is called upon to start, Johnson said he has confidence in the signal-caller. "He's wired the right way. Having a full week of preparation can make all the difference in performance," Johnson said of Bagent. "I said at the Combine, we view him as one of the top 32 (NFL quarterbacks). The way he approaches it, his teammates are going to fight their tails off for him." --Field Level Media

item.title: US halts flights at busy East Coast airports, says fiber line cut at construction site
item.description: The Federal Aviation Administration halted flights at busy East Coast airports in New York, Philadelphia and Boston on Monday, saying a fiber cable was accidentally cut at a construction site in New Jersey.
item.dc:creator: David Shepardson
item.content:encoded: The Federal Aviation Administration halted flights at busy East Coast airports in New York, Philadelphia and Boston on Monday, saying a fiber cable was accidentally cut at a construction site in New Jersey. Ground stops were issued for John F. Kennedy Airport and LaGuardia airports, as well as an airport in Teterboro, New Jersey, as 130 world leaders and dozens of ministers are arriving in New York for the annual high-level meeting of the United Nations General Assembly. FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford told reporters a backup fiber line had been cut accidentally by a construction crew in New Jersey, prompting significant flight cuts. He said a new circuit would be operational imminently. It was not clear when the ground stops at the New York-area airports would be lifted. FlightAware, a flight-tracking site, said more than 600 flights at Newark and Philadelphia, or more than 20%, had been delayed at Philadelphia Terminal Radar Approach Control. Newark is a major United Airlines (UAL.O) hub, while Philadelphia is an American Airlines (AAL.O) hub. The issue has also forced the diversion of a number of flights to other airports. Flightradar24, a flight-tracking site, said flights were being delayed by an average of 112 minutes at Newark. In May 2025, the facility that guides air traffic in and out of Newark airport suffered a series of significant communications outages. The FAA said last year a telecommunications outage impacted communications and radar displays at Philadelphia TRACON. Last year, Congress approved $12.5 billion to address the aging air traffic control system, and boost controller hiring following decades of complaints over airport congestion and flight delays and a series of technology issues in recent years.

item.title: US lawmakers urge Trump to maintain ban on Chinese automakers
item.description: More than two dozen Democratic lawmakers on Friday urged President Donald Trump to keep in place a ban on Chinese automakers out of the US market, ahead of his meeting with China's President Xi Jinping this week.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: More than two dozen Democratic lawmakers on Friday urged President Donald Trump to keep in place a ban on Chinese automakers out of the US market, ahead of his meeting with China's President Xi Jinping this week. "We urge you to maintain strong protections against Chinese automobiles and connected vehicle technologies and ensure that China does not gain access to our market through direct imports, local production, and other avenues of circumvention," said the 27 lawmakers led by Representative Debbie Dingell. Earlier this month, Trump told Fox News he would accept [USN:L1N45400M TEXT:"Chinese car companies"] building cars in the United States. (This story has been refiled to fix a typo in the headline.)

item.title: Patria Investimentos e unidade da Ashmore vendem usina solar na Colômbia para a Isagen
item.description: A gestora de ativos brasileira Patria Investmentos e a filial colombiana da gestora Ashmore Group anunciaram nesta segunda-feira que venderam uma usina de energia solar para a geradora Isagen, que tem a Brookfield Renewable como sua principal acionista.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A gestora de ativos brasileira Patria Investmentos (PAX.O) e a filial colombiana da gestora Ashmore Group (ASHM.L) anunciaram nesta segunda-feira que venderam uma usina de energia solar para a geradora Isagen, que tem a Brookfield Renewable (BEP.N) como sua principal acionista. A usina, chamada Puerta de Oro e localizada na região central da Colômbia, possui capacidade instalada de 360 MWp, com mais de 511.000 módulos distribuídos por 530 hectares. As empresas se recusaram a divulgar o preço de venda do parque solar. O projeto tem uma capacidade estimada de geração de 728 GWh de energia limpa por ano, o que equivale ao consumo de mais de 390.000 residências. “Puerta de Oro representa uma história de sucesso para o Patria e reflete nossa capacidade de identificar oportunidades, estruturar e desenvolver ativos de infraestrutura de alto impacto e gerar valor ao longo de todo o seu ciclo de investimento”, afirmou Pablo Cano, presidente-executivo de Infraestrutura do Patria Investmentos, em comunicado. Camilo Marulanda, presidente da Isagen, afirmou em comunicado que a inclusão de Puerta de Oro no portfólio da empresa representa um passo significativo rumo à meta de adicionar mais 1.000 MW de energia solar nos próximos anos. O BNP Paribas (BNPP.PA) atuou como consultor durante a transação. (Reportagem de Nelson Bocanegra, Texto de Paolo Laudani)

item.title: Lions DB Avonte Maddox to have season-ending foot surgery
item.description: Detroit Lions defensive back Avonte Maddox will have season-ending foot surgery, coach Dan Campbell confirmed Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Detroit Lions defensive back Avonte Maddox will have season-ending foot surgery, coach Dan Campbell confirmed Monday. The 30-year-old veteran injured his left foot during the second quarter of Thursday night's 41-31 loss at Buffalo. Maddox went down following a collision in the end zone with teammate Chuck Clark. He finishes his ninth NFL season with 10 tackles and two passes defensed in two starts for the Lions (1-1). Maddox has 312 tackles, five interceptions and nine forced fumbles in 97 career games with Philadelphia (2018-24) and Detroit (2025-26). He won a ring with the Eagles in Super Bowl LIX. The Lions were already short-handed in the secondary with star safeties Brian Branch (Achilles) and Kerby Joseph (knee) both starting the season on the reserve/physically unable to perform list. --Field Level Media

item.title: STOXX 600 repunta gracias a fortaleza de tecnológicas y de bancos, en medio descenso del crudo
item.description: El repunte de los grandes bancos y los valores tecnológicos impulsó las bolsas europeas el lunes, mientras los precios del petróleo caían por cuarta sesión consecutiva, reforzando el ánimo de riesgo general.
item.dc:creator: Sudeshna Ghoshal, Purvi Agarwal
item.content:encoded: El repunte de los grandes bancos y los valores tecnológicos impulsó las bolsas europeas el lunes, mientras los precios del petróleo caían por cuarta sesión consecutiva, reforzando el ánimo de riesgo general. El índice paneuropeo STOXX 600 (.STOXX) cerró con una subida del 1%, lo que supone su mayor alza diaria desde el 2 de julio. La mayoría de las bolsas regionales también avanzaron. Este movimiento supone un comienzo optimista de la semana, en el que los inversores evalúan si el retroceso del crudo puede aliviar las presiones inflacionarias. El Banco Central Europeo subió las tasas de interés este mes para combatir la inflación, ya que la fuerte dependencia de las importaciones de combustible deja a las economías regionales expuestas a las fluctuaciones de los precios del petróleo. "A pesar de los persistentes obstáculos y de una inflación superior al objetivo, el crecimiento económico debería repuntar en la segunda mitad del año, con unas perspectivas en Europa más sólidas de lo que espera el consenso", escribió Christian Schulz, economista jefe de Allianz Global Investors. Las acciones bancarias (.SX7P) se encontraron entre las que más subieron, con un alza del 1,7%. Société Générale (SOGN.PA) ganó un 1,7% y Banco BPM (BAMI.MI) , un 4,3%, este último tras las especulaciones de los medios sobre UniCredit (CRDI.MI) y Crédit Agricole (CAGR.PA) , que según se informa, estarían valorando una operación conjunta sobre la entidad crediticia italiana. Las acciones tecnológicas (.SX8P) sumaron un 1,7%, ya que el renovado interés por la inteligencia artificial impulsó a los valores relacionados con los chips, como Soitec (SOIT.PA) y Aixtron (AIXGn.DE) . Sin embargo, el sector energético (.SXEP) cayó un 0,8%, ya que los futuros del crudo Brent se encaminan a su racha más larga de pérdidas diarias desde junio, después de que algunos informes sugirieran que estaba saliendo del golfo un volumen de suministro superior al esperado, a pesar del conflicto en curso con Irán. El índice alemán DAX (.GDAXI) subió un 1,1%, mientras los inversores asimilaban los resultados de las elecciones regionales en el noreste de Alemania, donde las previsiones apuntaban a que el partido de extrema derecha Alternativa para Alemania se erigiría como la principal fuerza política. Mientras, Novo Nordisk (NOVOb.CO) fue la que más cayó en el STOXX 600, con un descenso del 7,7%, ya que sus directivos tuvieron que hacer frente a duras preguntas sobre el poder de fijación de precios y la estrategia de acuerdos de la farmacéutica ante la inminente expiración de patentes, durante la jornada de mercados de capitales de la empresa.

item.title: Nissan launches Tekton SUV in South Africa after plant closure
item.description: Nissan launched its new Tekton SUV in South Africa on Monday, betting that a wave of new vehicle introductions can help to revive growth and reassure customers and dealers after the Japanese automaker exited local manufacturing this year and shifted to an import-focused business.
item.dc:creator: Nqobile Dludla
item.content:encoded: Nissan (7201.T) launched its new Tekton SUV in South Africa on Monday, betting that a wave of new vehicle introductions can help to revive growth and reassure customers and dealers after the Japanese automaker exited local manufacturing this year and shifted to an import-focused business. The launch marks the first in a series of new models Nissan plans to bring to South Africa as it seeks to strengthen its presence in Africa's biggest automotive market after the [USN:L4N3YO0OK TEXT:"sale of its Pretoria plant"] this year to China's Chery (9973.HK) , a move that raised questions about the brand's future in the country. Nissan has been restructuring globally to cut costs through plant closures, job reductions and a leaner vehicle portfolio. "Unfortunately, we had to stop the activity of manufacturing in South Africa. We're maximising capacity in other plants, and that makes us more competitive, which hopefully we see in the vehicles we bring," Nissan Africa President Jordi Vila told reporters at the launch. South Africa's automotive sector is undergoing significant change as established global brands face growing competition from Chinese carmakers while adapting to shifting consumer demand towards SUVs and more affordable options. "It's designed to compete, it's designed to stay relevant and most of all it is designed to let South Africans fall in love again with the brand that has been part of our lives," Vila said, referring to the Tekton with a starting price of 339,999 rand ($20,939.64). The Tekton, which is manufactured in India, is being introduced in South Africa as Nissan's first African launch market for the model since its global debut in India and among the first launches worldwide. Nissan has already introduced a new X-Trail SUV in South Africa this year and plans to launch an upgraded Navara pick-up and the eighth-generation Patrol SUV during the current financial year. Further models are scheduled from next year. The company said it remained committed to South Africa despite ending local vehicle production.

item.title: Miami RB Marty Brown, WR Joshua Moore out for season
item.description: No. 6 Miami's 33-20 road win over Wake Forest last Friday proved costly on the injury front.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: No. 6 Miami's 33-20 road win over Wake Forest last Friday proved costly on the injury front. Running back Marty Brown and wide receiver Joshua Moore both will miss the rest of the season due to injuries, Hurricanes coach Mario Cristobal said Monday morning. Brown appeared to sustain a serious knee injury on a second-quarter carry, while Moore is dealing with an upper body injury, per Cristobal. Star running back Mark Fletcher Jr. and sophomore standout receiver Malachi Toney also sustained injuries during the Wake Forest win, as did defensive lineman Ahmad Moten Sr. and linebacker Ezekiel Marcelin Jr. Cristobal is optimistic about the injuries to Fletcher, Toney and Moten, while Marcelin will miss several weeks with a lower body injury. "We got banged up," Cristobal said Monday in a radio interview on WQAM 560 AM. "An interesting kind of situation." Brown trailed only Fletcher on last year's Miami team, which lost the national championship game, with 474 rushing yards and seven scores along with 138 receiving yards and two more touchdowns. He had 97 yards and one touchdown in three games this season. Moore had 210 receiving yards and two TDs last season as a freshman and was second on this year's squad with 107 receiving yards and two scores through three games. The Hurricanes (3-0) host Central Michigan on Saturday evening before returning to Atlantic Coast Conference play at Clemson on Oct. 3. --Field Level Media

item.title: China's GAC plans to launch 12 electric and hybrid models in France by 2030
item.description: Guangzhou Automobile Group plans to launch 12 electric and hybrid models in France by 2030, GAC France's deputy CEO Cedric Lacour said on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Guangzhou Automobile Group (601238.SS) plans to launch 12 electric and hybrid models in France by 2030, GAC France's deputy CEO Cedric Lacour said on Monday. GAC also plans to operate 50 dealerships this year in France, rising to 200 in 2030, he added. "Our goal is to take a brand from launch to scaling up in just four years," he said at the launch of GAC's two first car models on the French market.

item.title: Vusion annonce un CA en hausse de 34% au S1 et confirme ses perspectives
item.description: Vusion a annoncé lundi un bond de 34% de son chiffre d'affaires semestriel, à 820 millions d'euros.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Vusion (VU.PA) a annoncé lundi un bond de 34% de son chiffre d'affaires semestriel, à 820 millions d'euros. "La progression de près de 40% du revenu VAS (dont 73% pour les revenus VAS récurrents), qui atteint 15% du CA total, illustre une forte dynamique d'innovation et l'élargissement rapide de notre portefeuille de solutions", a déclaré Thierry Gadou, président-directeur général, dans un communiqué. Vusion a également fait état d'une hausse de 51% de son free cash-flow sur un an, celui-ci étant de 127 millions d'euros. Le groupe français spécialisé dans les systèmes électroniques d'étiquetage pour les supermarchés a confirmé ses perspectives pour 2026, dont une croissance du chiffre d’affaires de 15% à 20% à taux de change et droits de douane constants, un chiffre d’affaires VAS (services à valeur ajoutée)en hausse d’environ 40% et une marge d’Ebitda ajusté en hausse de plus de 100 points de base.

item.title: Grail rallies as FDA staff flags no major concerns for multi-cancer test
item.description: The US FDA's staff reviewers did not raise major concerns about the accuracy and safety of Grail's blood test designed to detect more than 50 cancers, sending the company's shares soaring 35% on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Christy Santhosh, Padmanabhan Ananthan
item.content:encoded: The US FDA's staff reviewers did not raise major concerns about the accuracy and safety of Grail's (GRAL.O) blood test designed to detect more than 50 cancers, sending the company's shares soaring 35% on Monday. The findings on the screening test, called Galleri, will be discussed at the FDA's external advisers' meeting on Wednesday to review Grail's request for premarket approval. The FDA has no outstanding questions for the external panel on analytical performance, study design and the primary safety analyses of Galleri, according to the briefing documents. But the agency asked the advisers to discuss whether the evidence supports Galleri's characterization as an "early detection" test. "We view this as constructive for Grail," said Piper Sandler analyst David Westenberg, adding that he expects a favorable vote. Grail's shares have plunged more than 20% since February after it said routine screening with the test [USN:L4N3ZG0RF TEXT:"failed"] to significantly boost early detection and reduce late-stage diagnoses in a pivotal three-year UK trial. The company had filed for the Food and Drug Administration's approval in January based on data from a smaller US trial, first-year data from the UK trial and a bridging analysis comparing data from an earlier version of the test. Galleri and Abbott Laboratories' (ABT.N) multi-cancer blood test, Cancerguard, are already available on the market under the Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments regulations, but neither is FDA-approved. An FDA approval ensures widespread distribution, adoption of guidelines for physicians and routine health insurance coverage. Multi-cancer early detection tests analyze molecular signals shed by tumors into the bloodstream from a single blood draw. Galleri is meant to complement, not replace, established screenings such as mammograms and colonoscopies, Grail has said. The test brought in revenue of $136.8 million in the US in 2025.

item.title: POINT MARCHÉS L'Europe finit en nette hausse, le Moyen-Orient suscite des espoirs
item.description: Les Bourses européennes ont terminé en nette hausse lundi, portées par les espoirs d'avancées diplomatiques au Moyen-Orient, en plus du recul des cours pétroliers.
item.dc:creator: Coralie Lamarque
item.content:encoded: Les Bourses européennes ont terminé en nette hausse lundi, portées par les espoirs d'avancées diplomatiques au Moyen-Orient, en plus du recul des cours pétroliers. À Paris, le CAC 40 (.FCHI) a gagné 0,92% à 8.138,94 points. À Francfort, le Dax (.GDAXI) a avancé de 1,07% et à Londres, le FTSE 100 (.FTSE) a pris 0,75%. L'indice EuroStoxx 50 (.STOXX50E) a progressé de 1,31%, le FTSEurofirst 300 (.FTEU3) de 1,04% et le Stoxx 600 (.STOXX) de 1,04%. La séance a été rythmée par le regain d'espoirs au Moyen-Orient, face à l'apaisement des craintes concernant l'approvisionnement en pétrole, conjugué aux perspectives d'avancées diplomatiques pour espérer mettre fin au conflit qui dure depuis fin février et dont les répercussions éreintent les marchés. Les données satellitaires montrent que le volume de pétrole saoudien transitant par le détroit d’Ormuz s’élevait en moyenne à 2,9 millions de barils par jour au cours des six derniers jours, contre seulement 700.000 barils par jour en août. Sur le plan diplomatique se tient cette semaine l’Assemblée générale des Nations unies (AGNU), au cours de laquelle Donald Trump déclare qu'il pourrait rencontrer le président iranien Massoud Pezeshkian. La prudence reste toutefois de mise face aux menaces persistantes sur le terrain, les Houthis du Yémen s’efforçant d’isoler la côte de la mer Rouge des zones encore contrôlées par les forces soutenues par l’Arabie saoudite. Par ailleurs, des sources [USN:L8N45D17K TEXT:"ont indiqué"] à Reuters que le président américain s'était entretenu dimanche par téléphone avec son homologue yéménite Rachad al Alimi, qui a sollicité l'aide militaire des États-Unis, sans que le président américain ne prenne d'engagement direct. Outre le Moyen-Orient, les investisseurs attendent également la rencontre entre Donald Trump et le président chinois Xi Jinping, espérant une prolongation de leur trêve commerciale, qui doit prendre fin le 10 novembre. En ce début de semaine, l'agenda des indicateurs économiques reste calme, avant les indices des directeurs d'achat (PMI) mercredi. "La publication des indicateurs d’activité PMI européens n’aura qu’un faible intérêt, car ils ne prennent pas pleinement en compte la problématique énergétique, qui redevient centrale", a déclaré Christopher Dembik, conseiller en stratégie d'investissement chez Pictet AM, dans une note. Par ailleurs, l'inflation en Allemagne devrait rester élevée pendant un certain temps en raison de la hausse des coûts énergétiques liée au conflit au Moyen-Orient et des réformes du système de santé prévues pour 2027, [USN:L6N45D0H4 TEXT:"a déclaré"] la Bundesbank dans son rapport mensuel. VALEURS Ipsen (IPN.PA) a perdu 5,13%, le laboratoire français se trouvant pénalisé par l'approbation aux États-Unis d'un générique concurrent de son médicament phare, Somatuline, une forme de lanréotide utilisée pour traiter l'acromégalie, les tumeurs neuroendocrines gastro-intestinales et pancréatiques et le syndrome carcinoïde. Ayvens (AYV.PA) recule de 2,0% après avoir annoncé prévoir une rentabilité des fonds propres tangibles (ROTE) comprise entre 14% et 16% en 2029, le groupe de location automobile présentant ses nouveaux objectifs stratégiques alors que s'achève l'exécution de son plan précédent, "PowerUP 2026". Société Générale (SOGN.PA) a progressé de 1,7% après avoir relevé son objectif de rentabilité pour 2029. À WALL STREET Au moment de la clôture en Europe, Wall Street reste dans le vert, le Dow Jones (.DJI) avançant de 0,46%, le Standard & Poor's 500 (.SPX) de 1,13% et le Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) de 1,71%. CHANGES Le billet vert progresse alors que les marchés évaluent la probabilité d'une nouvelle hausse des taux par la Fed. Le dollar gagne 0,18% face à un panier de devises de référence (.DXY) , tandis que l'euro perd 0,13% à 1,1468 dollar . TAUX Sous tension, le marché obligataire tente une désescalade avec le repli des cours pétroliers. Le rendement des Treasuries à dix ans recule de 3,5 points de base à 4,9613%. Le deux ans cède 0,5 point de base à 4,7376%. Le rendement du Bund allemand à dix ans est resté inchangé à 3,4526%. Le deux ans a lâché 0,7 point de base à 3,1978%. PÉTROLE Les cours pétroliers reculent et le Brent repasse sous la barre des 100 dollars le baril, face aux espoirs d'avancées diplomatiques et concernant les exportations saoudiennes. Le Brent perd 3,75% à 99,98 dollars le baril et le brut léger américain (West Texas Intermediate, WTI) recule de 4,58% à 95,71 dollars. item.title: German institutes raise 2026 and 2027 economic growth forecasts, Handelsblatt reports
item.description: Germany's leading economic institutes have raised their forecasts for economic growth in Europe's largest economy for this year and next, Handelsblatt reported on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Germany's leading economic institutes have raised their forecasts for economic growth in Europe's largest economy for this year and next, Handelsblatt reported on Monday. The German economy is forecast to grow 1.3% in 2026, compared with an earlier forecast of 0.6%, Handelsblatt reported citing unnamed sources. For 2027, they forecast growth of 1.1%, up from an earlier forecast of 0.9%. Germany's sluggish economy has been a big issue in the [USN:L8N45C0DZ TEXT:"country's recent elections"] that have resulted in big gains for the far right and far left. The forecasts are a joint effort by five prominent economic institutes - RWI in Essen, the Ifo institute in Munich, IfW in Kiel, IWH in Halle and DIW in Berlin. They didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.

item.title: Newsom signs bill limiting investor influence in California law firms
item.description: California, one of the largest US legal markets, has joined Colorado and Illinois in enacting legislation to limit investor influence in law firms amid surging interest in deals that allow outside capital to fuel lawyers' business.
item.dc:creator: David Thomas
item.content:encoded: California, one of the largest US legal markets, has joined Colorado and [USN:L6N4470UV TEXT:"Illinois"] in enacting legislation to limit investor influence in law firms amid surging interest in deals that allow outside capital to fuel lawyers' business. California Governor Gavin Newsom on Sunday signed legislation prohibiting business entities from interfering or attempting to "influence the professional judgment of a licensed attorney or litigant regarding any substantive litigation decision," including lawyers' settlement decisions and what cases and clients they take. Violators, including attorney recipients of outside capital, face statutory damages of $10,000 per violation, or three times the damages suffered by a client. California Assembly member Ash Kalra, who authored AB 2305, did not immediately respond to a request for comment. In a statement last month, Kalra said, "The principle is simple: when you hire a lawyer, the person making decisions about your case should be your lawyer — not a private equity entity looking for profit." Consumer Attorneys of California, a trade group that backed the legislation, said in a statement Monday that the state is "setting the standard for the rest of the country to follow." Investors and other non-lawyers are broadly prohibited in the United States from owning direct stakes in law firms or sharing in attorney fees. However, a growing number of firms are inking deals to spin off their non-legal, back-office operations like human resources or marketing into a separate organization called a management services organization (MSO), that is owned or partly owned by outside investors. Such deals can provide an influx of capital for a law firm, which pays the MSO from its revenues but does not share fees. Some MSOs serve multiple firms. California's new law applies to business entities that raise or manage capital and are involved in litigation practice "no matter how it is legally structured, labeled, organized, or operated." Newsom last year [USN:L2N3VV010 TEXT:"signed into law a bill"] that prohibited attorneys in the state from splitting fees with out-of-state "alternative business structures," unless there is a contract stating that the fees will be shared, as well as other conditions.
