item.title: Justicia argentina procesa a ocho iraníes y libaneses por ataque antijudío de los 90
item.description: La Justicia argentina informó el lunes que procesó a un ciudadano libanés y a siete iraníes acusados de participar en un ataque terrorista a una entidad judía que dejó 85 muertos en Buenos Aires en 1994.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La Justicia argentina informó el lunes que procesó a un ciudadano libanés y a siete iraníes acusados de participar en un ataque terrorista a una entidad judía que dejó 85 muertos en Buenos Aires en 1994. El caso del ataque contra la Asociación Mutual Israelita Argentina (AMIA), que nunca fue esclarecido, tuvo muchos avances y retrocesos a lo largo de los años, lo que derivó en un juicio en ausencia de los acusados por el atentado. "La decisión de cometer el atentado fue adoptada en agosto de 1993 por parte de las máximas instancias del régimen iraní y encomendada a Hezbollah", señaló el juez federal Daniel Rafecas en una resolución a la que accedió Reuters. Según el documento, los procesados son los exfuncionarios iraníes Alí Fallahijan, Alí Velayati, Mohsen Rezai, Ahmad Vahidi, Hadi Soleimanpour, Mohsen Rabbani y Ahmad Asghari, junto al agente libanés de Hezbollah Salman Raouf Salman. Los hombres, acusados por los delitos de homicidios y lesiones agravados por el odio racial o religioso, se mantienen prófugos fuera de Argentina.

item.title: Mercados financieros de Argentina operan en baja, comitiva FMI visita el país para revisión programa
item.description: La plaza financiera argentina operaba mayormente en baja el lunes, con una marcada reducción de negocios, en momentos en que los inversores centran su atención en la visita de una misión del Fondo Monetario Internacional (FMI) para la tercera revisión del programa de 20.000 millones de dólares con el país.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La plaza financiera argentina operaba mayormente en baja el lunes, con una marcada reducción de negocios, en momentos en que los inversores centran su atención en la visita de una misión del Fondo Monetario Internacional (FMI) para la tercera revisión del programa de 20.000 millones de dólares con el país. "Una nueva misión del FMI en Argentina comienza hoy para llevar a cabo la tercera revisión del programa, que determinaría si Argentina recibe un nuevo desembolso de 870 millones de dólares por parte del organismo", dijo la consultora Max Capital. Fuentes del Ministerio de Economía consultadas por Reuters no hicieron declaraciones sobre la visita de los funcionarios del organismo. El FMI declaró recientemente que la tercera economía de América Latina debe seguir [USN:L1N4520OO TEXT:"fortaleciendo sus reservas"], reducir riesgos financieros y mantener el ancla fiscal. Con el fin de reforzar sus arcas, el banco central argentino mantiene compras de divisas en el mercado cambiario pero a un ritmo menor al de meses previos, según operadores. En lo que va de septiembre, la entidad monetaria acumula adquisiciones de divisas por unos 203 millones de dólares, luego de que en agosto sumara compras por unos 770 millones de dólares. En el año totaliza unos 14.260 millones de dólares. "Las compras acumuladas (del BCRA) del mes alcanzan apenas 205 millones de dólares, cuando restan ocho ruedas para cerrar septiembre. Esto implica un promedio de solo 15 millones de dólares por día, muy por debajo de los 170 millones diarios que, en promedio, viene liquidando el agro", dijo la consultora Portfolio Personal Inversiones (PPI). "La liquidación del agro en septiembre sería la mayor para este mes (...). Entonces, si el agro está vendiendo a este ritmo y el BCRA compra tan poco, ¿quién se lleva la diferencia? El resto de los sectores representa una demanda neta de unos 154 millones de dólares por rueda en lo que va del mes", añadió. "En consecuencia, el BCRA ha tenido que ajustar significativamente sus compras para que el tipo de cambio se mantenga prácticamente inalterado", remarcó PPI. El peso argentino en la plaza interbancaria se depreciaba un 0,07% a 1.516 unidades por dólar para la venta. Por su parte, el índice líder S&P Merval (.MERV) de la Bolsa de Buenos Aires perdía un 0,61% a las 1435 GMT, tras finalizar la semana previa con una merma de un 2,48%. Operadores señalaron que la reducción de operaciones en los mercados argentinos se veía afectada por la celebración del "Yom Kippur", una fecha de gran relevancia en el calendario judío que provoca la ausencia de operadores y ahorristas. Los bonos en el segmento extrabursátil mejoraban un 0,2% promedio y el riesgo país se ubicaba en 521 puntos básicos.

item.title: Russia will have budget deficit not exceeding 3% of GDP in 2026, Finance Minister says
item.description: Russia will have a budget deficit equal to 3% of gross domestic product in 2026, almost double the plan and more than last year, Finance Minister Anton Siluanov said on Monday as the government prepares to review the draft of the 2027 budget this week.
item.dc:creator: Darya Korsunskaya, Elena Fabrichnaya
item.content:encoded: Russia will have a budget deficit equal to 3% of gross domestic product in 2026, almost double the plan and more than last year, Finance Minister Anton Siluanov said on Monday as the government prepares to review the draft of the 2027 budget this week. Russia hiked taxes this year to cope with the rising expenditure to finance the military action in Ukraine, hoping to reduce the budget deficit to 1.6% of GDP from 2.6% in 2025, but the current deficit in January-August already stands at 2.5% of GDP. "Certainly, during the execution of the budget, additional needs for funding and expenditures have arisen. Additional sources of funding for these expenditures will be provided for this purpose," Siluanov told Russian state television. This year, Russia had to boost its air defences as Ukraine carried out successful drone attacks on economic infrastructure such as refineries, ports and e-commerce warehouses, as well as spending on measures to ease nationwide fuel shortages. The deficit this year rose despite increased revenues from export of oil as global prices rose on the war in the Middle East as well as a weakening rouble, which generally helps the budget, inflating state revenues from exports. Siluanov said that the government will plan to borrow more than the initially planned 5.5 trillion roubles ($65.7 billion) and use some leftover funds from previous years to finance the deficit. He said that additional borrowing by the state did not pose risks for the financial system. President Vladimir Putin [USN:L1N4590S4 TEXT:"said"] last week that the deficit for 2027 is expected to fall to about 2% and that he expected oil and gas revenues to increase in the coming months. Siluanov said that such a deficit would create room for further easing of monetary policy. "The main thing is that we have coordinated with the central bank. What is important today? It is important that our inflation, inflation expectations, and interest rates fall," Siluanov said. Russia has a low overall state debt but servicing costs have been increasing due to high interest rates. The central bank, which had mentioned the budget situation as one of the factors in its rate-setting decisions, said on Monday the current deficit projections were in line with its expectations. Siluanov said that fiscal reserves at the National Wealth Fund, whose gradual depletion was seen by analysts as one of the key risks for the budget, will rise by between 600 billion and 1 trillion roubles to 5 trillion roubles by the end of 2026. ($1 = 83.7455 roubles)

item.title: Banco Mundial y FMI respaldan los cambios en el marco de deuda para los países pobres
item.description: El Banco Mundial y el Fondo Monetario Internacional anunciaron el lunes que sus respectivos consejos ejecutivos habían aprobado las reformas propuestas para su marco conjunto de evaluación de la deuda de los países de bajos ingresos, con el fin de reflejar un entorno más complejo y arriesgado.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El Banco Mundial y el Fondo Monetario Internacional anunciaron el lunes que sus respectivos consejos ejecutivos habían aprobado las reformas propuestas para su marco conjunto de evaluación de la deuda de los países de bajos ingresos, con el fin de reflejar un entorno más complejo y arriesgado. Una revisión conjunta, la primera desde 2017, recomendó cambios en varios ámbitos, entre ellos un mejor análisis de la deuda interna y la ampliación del análisis de los retos de desarrollo a largo plazo, incluido el cambio climático. Las reformas contribuirán a mejorar el análisis de los riesgos para la sostenibilidad de la deuda, perfeccionando la forma en que se mide la capacidad de los países para soportar la deuda e introduciendo nuevas herramientas para evaluar dicha sostenibilidad. Por último, el Banco Mundial y el FMI trabajarán para mejorar las "herramientas de realismo" y las pruebas de resistencia utilizadas para garantizar la coherencia y la precisión de las previsiones, al tiempo que animarán a los países a mejorar la transparencia de los datos sobre la deuda, según ha indicado el Banco Mundial. El FMI y el Banco Mundial utilizan el marco de sostenibilidad de la deuda para analizar y evaluar la capacidad de un país para contraer nueva deuda sin poner en peligro su capacidad para hacer frente al servicio de los préstamos existentes. Se recomendaron estos cambios dado que muchos países de bajos ingresos han experimentado un aumento de los niveles de deuda y un cambio en las fuentes de financiación, que ahora incluyen un mayor recurso al endeudamiento interno y externo en condiciones comerciales. Se espera que el marco revisado entre en vigor en el segundo semestre de 2027, añadió. Una revisión finalizada en julio confirmó que el marco de sostenibilidad de la deuda había funcionado bien a la hora de identificar con antelación episodios de sobreendeudamiento y ayudar a los países a tomar decisiones informadas sobre la obtención y la concesión de préstamos.

item.title: Peso mexicano se estabiliza cerca de máximos de un mes y medio
item.description: El peso mexicano se estabilizaba el lunes cerca de sus máximos de un mes y medio, debido a la cautela de los inversionistas al comienzo de una semana dominada localmente por la decisión de política monetaria del banco central.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El peso mexicano se estabilizaba el lunes cerca de sus máximos de un mes y medio, debido a la cautela de los inversionistas al comienzo de una semana dominada localmente por la decisión de política monetaria del [USN:L1N4510I3 TEXT:"banco central"]. El mercado espera que el Banco de México mantenga sin cambios su tasa de referencia durante un periodo prolongado, pese a que la [USN:L1N4580T6 TEXT:"Reserva Federal"] elevó las tasas de interés la semana pasada y señaló que podrían venir nuevos ajustes. * La moneda local cotizaba en 17.2250 por dólar, con pocos cambios frente a las 17.2210 unidades del precio de referencia de LSEG del viernes, mientras los mercados también se preparaban para una batería de datos económicos de Estados Unidos esta semana. * "Seguiremos las cifras preliminares del índice de gerentes de compras (PMI, por sus siglas en inglés) en busca de señales de que la actividad empresarial resiste el aumento de los costos de endeudamiento", dijo BlackRock en un reporte. "La resiliencia de Estados Unidos reforzaría el argumento a favor de tasas más altas durante más tiempo", agregó. * En esa línea, el presidente de la Fed de Chicago, [USN:L6N45D0IJ TEXT:"Austan Goolsbee"], afirmó que está abierto a la posibilidad de que la inflación comience a descender hacia el objetivo. Sin embargo, advirtió que, de no ocurrir, sería necesario subir las tasas de interés. * Por lo pronto, el [USN:L6N45D0F6 TEXT:"dólar estadounidense"] se estabilizaba frente a una cesta de divisas y los [USN:L6N45D0F7 TEXT:"precios del petróleo"] tocaban su menor nivel en 11 días, ante expectativas de avances diplomáticos sobre Irán durante la [USN:L6N45D05O TEXT:"Asamblea General de la ONU"] y una recuperación parcial de los envíos desde Arabia Saudita. * Los operadores aguardaban, además, señales de una esperada reunión esta semana entre el presidente estadounidense, Donald Trump, y su homólogo chino, [USN:L6N45D09X TEXT:"Xi Jinping"], quien visitaría Estados Unidos del 23 al 25 de septiembre para mantener conversaciones bilaterales. * En el mercado accionario, el índice líder S&P/BMV IPC (.MXX) subía un 0.24% a 63,525.71 puntos, después de tocar nuevos mínimos del año. * Los títulos del conglomerado Grupo Carso GCARSOA1.MX> encabezaban las alzas, con un 3.59% más a 134.44 pesos, seguidos por los de la aerolínea Volaris (VOLARA.MX) , que avanzaban un 2.57% a 11.58 pesos. * En el mercado secundario de deuda, el rendimiento del bono gubernamental a 10 años descendía cuatro puntos base, a un 9.41%, igual que la tasa a 20 años que se ubicaba en un 9.85%.

item.title: Banco Mundial e FMI aprovam reformas no quadro de avaliação da dívida de países pobres
item.description: O Banco Mundial e o Fundo Monetário Internacional (FMI) anunciaram nesta segunda-feira que seus conselhos executivos aprovaram as reformas propostas para o quadro conjunto de avaliação da dívida de países de baixa renda, a fim de refletir um ambiente mais complexo e arriscado.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O Banco Mundial e o Fundo Monetário Internacional (FMI) anunciaram nesta segunda-feira que seus conselhos executivos aprovaram as reformas propostas para o quadro conjunto de avaliação da dívida de países de baixa renda, a fim de refletir um ambiente mais complexo e arriscado. Uma revisão conjunta, a primeira desde 2017, recomendou mudanças em várias áreas, incluindo uma análise mais aprofundada da dívida interna e a ampliação da análise dos desafios de desenvolvimento de longo prazo, abarcando as mudanças climáticas. As reformas visam melhorar a análise dos riscos à sustentabilidade da dívida, aperfeiçoando a forma como a capacidade de endividamento dos países é medida e introduzindo novas ferramentas para avaliar a sustentabilidade. Por fim, o Banco Mundial e o FMI trabalharão para aprimorar as “ferramentas de realismo” e os testes de estresse utilizados para garantir a consistência e a precisão das previsões, ao mesmo tempo em que incentivam os países a melhorar a transparência dos dados sobre a dívida, informou o Banco Mundial. O FMI e o Banco Mundial utilizam a estrutura de sustentabilidade da dívida para analisar e avaliar a capacidade de um país de contrair mais crédito sem comprometer sua capacidade de honrar os empréstimos existentes. As mudanças foram recomendadas, uma vez que muitos países de baixa renda têm enfrentado níveis crescentes de endividamento e uma mudança nas fontes de financiamento, passando a incluir mais empréstimos internos e externos em condições comerciais. Espera-se que o quadro revisado entre em vigor no segundo semestre de 2027, acrescentou a instituição. Uma revisão concluída em julho confirmou que o quadro de sustentabilidade da dívida havia funcionado bem para identificar antecipadamente episódios de sobreendividamento e ajudar os países a tomar decisões informadas sobre empréstimos e financiamentos. No entanto, a análise também identificou várias áreas em que o quadro poderia ser aprimorado para levar em conta novos desafios.

item.title: China making progress on finalizing Boeing purchases announced in May
item.description: China is making progress on a commitment to buy 200 Boeing jets it announced in May, U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said on Monday.
item.dc:creator: David Shepardson
item.content:encoded: China is making progress on a commitment to buy 200 Boeing (BA.N) jets it announced in May, U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said on Monday. Greer gave no indication that any additional Chinese airplane orders for Boeing are near ahead of President Donald Trump's meeting this week with Chinese President Xi Jinping. "There are about 140 that are in a good state. There are an additional 10 that are they're writing down the orders," Greer told Fox News of the Boeing orders for Chinese carriers. The orders marked Boeing's first major Chinese deal in nearly a decade. In May, Trump said China could potentially boost its Boeing order to as many as 750 planes. Boeing CEO Kelly Ortberg last week played down some expectations among industry analysts that China could make another Boeing order around the Trump-Xi talks. "I think there’ll be an increment of orders going forward," Ortberg said at an investor conference. "They’re going to be announced by the airlines at their pace, however they want to announce those." Ortberg said in May that the 200 airplane order commitment by China was only an "initial tranche" of a potentially far bigger deal.

item.title: Report: Saints OT Kelvin Banks Jr. to have ankle surgery
item.description: New Orleans Saints left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. is scheduled to undergo ankle surgery and will be out indefinitely, NFL Network reported Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: New Orleans Saints left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. is scheduled to undergo ankle surgery and will be out indefinitely, NFL Network reported Monday. Banks, 22, was carted off late in the third quarter of a 24-17 victory over the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday. An MRI on Monday confirmed a severe high ankle sprain, according to the report. Banks is now set to miss game action for the first time since New Orleans selected him ninth overall in the 2025 NFL Draft. He started all 17 games last year as a rookie and started the first two games this season. Asim Richards, 25, replaced Banks and will likely step into the starting lineup in his absence. A fifth-round draft pick by Dallas in 2023, Richards has played in 38 games (five starts) over the last four seasons. The Saints (1-1) are scheduled to face the Las Vegas Raiders in their home opener Sunday. --Field Level Media

item.title: UK charges man over alleged Rwanda genocide offences
item.description: A 65-year-old Rwandan man has been charged with genocide-related offences allegedly committed during the 1994 Rwanda Tutsi killings, British prosecutors said on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A 65-year-old Rwandan man has been charged with genocide-related offences allegedly committed during the 1994 Rwanda Tutsi killings, British prosecutors said on Monday. Vincent Brown, formerly known as Vincent Bajinya, was charged with one offence of conduct ancillary to genocide and six offences of conduct ancillary to murder as a crime against humanity. Britain's Counter Terrorism Policing War Crimes Team said Brown was accused of encouraging others to kill Tutsis in Kigali in April 1994. The investigation began in 2019 following a request from the Rwandan government and involved years of international cooperation, it added. Brown was accused of having "directed and incited acts of murder and genocide carried out by others", the Crown Prosecution Service said. The charges against Brown were the first brought in the United Kingdom relating to the Rwandan genocide, the CPS added. Brown, who is remanded in custody, is due to appear at London's Westminster Magistrates' Court on Tuesday. Police said investigations into six other individuals remain ongoing, including two men arrested in 2024 and 2026 on suspicion of genocide and crimes against humanity who remain on bail. More than 800,000 Tutsis and moderate Hutus were killed in 100 days in the 1994 genocide, orchestrated by the Hutu ruling majority and meticulously executed by local officials and ordinary citizens.

item.title: Litigation funder Burford resolves lawsuit against client in price-fixing cases
item.description: Litigation funder Burford Capital has reached a settlement with one of its funding clients, food distributor Harvest Sherwood, whose bankruptcy last year complicated Burford's efforts to recoup a $35 million investment.
item.dc:creator: Mike Scarcella
item.content:encoded: Litigation funder Burford Capital (BURF.L) has reached a settlement with one of its funding clients, food distributor Harvest Sherwood, whose bankruptcy last year complicated Burford's efforts to recoup a $35 million investment. Here are the details: Publicly-traded Burford is the world’s largest litigation finance provider. Litigation funders provide financial support to clients in exchange for a part of any settlement or judgment. In a court filing , Burford affiliates including Blakemore Investments on Thursday agreed to end their lawsuit in federal district court in Texas against Harvest Sherwood and affiliates, including Hamilton Meat. Burford will be paid $9.5 million in a settlement with Harvest, court papers show. Detroit-based Harvest Sherwood in 2022 borrowed $35 million from Burford to help fund antitrust lawsuits accusing major meat processors of illegally fixing prices. Once the country’s largest independent wholesale food distributors, Harvest Sherwood declared bankruptcy in May 2025. Its antitrust lawsuits accusing pork, chicken and beef producers of illegally fixing prices are among the company's key remaining assets. Blakemore sued Harvest, Hamilton and other defendants as part of the bankruptcy last year. The complaint said the agreement to fund antitrust claims worth as much as $1.1 billion made Burford a secured creditor in the bankruptcy with a first-priority right to proceeds from the cases. Harvest Sherwood said the funders sought improperly to “elevate Burford’s unsecured claim to some amorphous senior and first priority interest.” Last November, Chief Judge Stacey Jernigan of the US Bankruptcy Court in Dallas had concluded Blakemore and another Burford entity had not shown that their capital provision agreement entitled them to payment ahead of secured creditors such as JPMorgan Chase. Burford declined to comment on the settlement. Lawyers for Harvest and Hamilton did not immediately respond to a request for comment. They said in court filings that the settlement with Burford is “fair, equitable and reasonable.” The case is Blakemore Investments LLC et al v. Hamilton Meat LLC et al, US District Court for the Northern District of Texas, No. 3:25-cv-03325-K. For Blakemore: Julian Vasek and Kevin Lippman of Munsch Hardt Kopf & Harr For Hamilton: Scott Cargill and Andrew Matott of Kelley Drye & Warren

item.title: Far-left leader pushing to lead Berlin says city has voted for change
item.description: The far-left leader pushing to take over as mayor of Berlin promised on Monday to tackle unaffordable rents in the German capital, but faced early pressure to take action over accusations of antisemitism in parts of the local party.
item.dc:creator: James Mackenzie
item.content:encoded: The far-left leader pushing to take over as mayor of Berlin promised on Monday to tackle unaffordable rents in the German capital, but faced early pressure to take action over accusations of antisemitism in parts of the local party. Elif Eralp led the Left Party to their best result in Berlin where they displaced Chancellor Friedrich Merz's conservative party in the mayor's office and look set to head a coalition governing the city for the first time. "Berlin has clearly voted in favour of a change in policy, for an affordable Berlin where everyone can live with dignity, regardless of income or background, and for the rent crisis to be tackled consistently at long last," she said on Monday. PLAN TARGETS CORPORATE LANDLORDS Famously described by former mayor Klaus Wowereit as "poor but sexy", Berlin has become increasingly expensive and its once famously cheap rents are now a thing of the past. Eralp has pledged to expropriate more than 200,000 housing units from corporate landlords in a campaign which saw the party, whose roots lie in the former East German communist party, make gains in central and western areas of the city as well as its traditional strongholds in the east. "I still stand by that," she said on Monday, despite questions about how to finance a move the centre-left Social Democrats estimated would cost some €20 billion ($22.94 billion). She said she aimed to reduce the influence of corporate landlords such as Deutsche Wohnen (DWNG.DE) and Vonovia (VNAn.DE) . Vonovia Chief Executive Luka Mucic said the group was ready to discuss solutions to Berlin's housing shortage but that "socialisation doesn't create any new housing". Merz, who said the policy would have "devastating effects" on foreign investment if it were ever implemented, said he expected swift legislation to prevent expropriations. MAMDANI AN EXAMPLE Compared by some to New York mayor Zohran Mamdani, whose campaign to make the city more affordable saw him win an unexpected victory last year, the 45-year-old Eralp is the child of left-wing Turkish parents who sought asylum in Germany after a military coup in 1980. Like Mamdani, her campaign focused heavily on personal campaigning and social media and she scored particularly strongly among the young, while winning support from thousands of Berliners who previously did not vote. "As a woman, I'm reluctant to compare myself to a man. But naturally Mamdani's success was a big example for us," she said. "And we were very happy about it, because that election victory sent a very clear signal — not just to New York, but to the entire world." Little known outside left-wing circles before the campaign, she now stands poised to lead the German capital at a time when the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) has made increasing gains across the country and posted its best-ever result in liberal Berlin. Potential coalition partners in the centre-left Social Democrats and the environmental Greens have indicated they are ready to talk about forming a government. But both have demanded Eralp address the longstanding accusations over antisemitism that have been levelled against some local branches of the Berlin party, often in connection with criticism of Israel. The issue has been extremely sensitive in Germany, which has seen a surge in antisemitic incidents since the October 7, 2023 attack on Israel by the militant group Hamas and the Israeli campaign that has laid waste to Gaza and killed tens of thousands. Merz said the rise in antisemitism was a "disgrace for Germany" and pledged action to combat incidents in Berlin that he said had caused concern to European partners. Eralp said it was her "absolute priority" to ensure that Jewish people in Berlin along with Muslims and all other groups "feel safe and can lead a good life here". "It is absolutely clear to me that the glorification of violence and terrorism is completely unacceptable," Eralp told a news conference. ($1 = 0.8718 euros)

item.title: EXCLUSIVA El BID elabora un plan de dos años para Venezuela; la electricidad y las necesidades sociales son clave
item.description: El Banco Interamericano de Desarrollo (BID) está elaborando un plan de colaboración a dos años para Venezuela, centrado inicialmente en la electricidad y la protección social, mientras evalúa las necesidades económicas y de inversión del país, dijo el lunes el presidente del BID, Ilan Goldfajn.
item.dc:creator: Rodrigo Campos
item.content:encoded: El Banco Interamericano de Desarrollo (BID) está elaborando un plan de colaboración a dos años para Venezuela, centrado inicialmente en la electricidad y la protección social, mientras evalúa las necesidades económicas y de inversión del país, dijo el lunes el presidente del BID, Ilan Goldfajn. "Por supuesto, estamos retomando la relación", declaró Goldfajn a Reuters en una entrevista. "Estamos enviando misiones a Venezuela para evaluar la situación, abordar el marco macroeconómico, analizar los datos y elaborar una nota de trabajo: un documento en el que podamos definir qué planeamos hacer en los próximos dos años". El BID es el mayor organismo multilateral de crédito para el desarrollo en América Latina y el Caribe y cuenta con 48 países miembros, incluidos 26 países prestatarios de la región. La institución dejó de otorgar nuevos préstamos a Venezuela en mayo de 2018, después de que el país incurriera en impagos, y aún mantiene una cartera de préstamos pendientes con Venezuela por valor de unos 2.000 millones de dólares. Goldfajn no precisó cómo se abordarían los atrasos en los pagos de Venezuela ni cuándo podría reanudarse la financiación. La televisora estatal venezolana mostró cerca del mediodía imágenes de una reunión de Goldfajn con la presidenta encargada, Delcy Rodríguez, quien arribó el lunes a Nueva York, pero no hubo transmisión de declaraciones de ese encuentro. "Todavía estamos en una fase de planificación y trabajo con los venezolanos; estamos estableciendo contactos, realizando misiones y viendo cómo podemos colaborar con ellos", señaló. Al ser consultado sobre si el BID estaba preparando su propio análisis de sostenibilidad de la deuda para Venezuela, Goldfajn indicó que, en cambio, se están centrando en el marco macroeconómico del país y en las necesidades de los distintos sectores.

item.title: Energy Watch: The Hormuz shuttle
item.description: The two conflicts that have dominated global energy markets are settling into a grim and costly stalemate, with neither showing any sign of a breakthrough.
item.dc:creator: Ron Bousso
item.content:encoded: The two conflicts that have dominated global energy markets are settling into a grim and costly stalemate, with neither showing any sign of a breakthrough. In Russia, Ukraine launched what was reported to be its [USN:FWN45A0G8 TEXT:"largest drone attack"] yet on the Moscow region, killing three people and damaging part of an oil refinery in the Russian capital. Russia, meanwhile, has intensified its bombardment of Ukrainian cities, making recent weeks among the deadliest of the war. In the Middle East, Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis fired missiles and drones toward the Saudi capital after making significant gains in the country's renewed civil war earlier this month. At the same time, Washington and Tehran [USN:L8N45C04D TEXT:"exchanged threats"]. President Donald Trump warned that Iran would face economic collapse, or even the destruction of its leadership, unless it strikes a deal with the United States, and Iran's military responded by vowing severe retaliation against any new attack. Despite the volatile geopolitical backdrop, Brent crude extended last week's losses on Monday, slipping to around $101 a barrel. The surprising calm is largely due to a development around the Strait of Hormuz. A new shuttling system is reshaping the Middle East oil market, as producers seek to keep exports flowing despite the escalating regional conflict . The question is whether this complex, expensive process is a stopgap measure or the global energy market’s new normal. Several miles off Oman's coast, south of the [USN:L4N45A04U TEXT:"Strait of Hormuz"], rows of tankers lie at anchor. Many sit alongside each other, connected by ropes and hoses as they transfer crude from one vessel to another, creating a floating bridge between the Middle East's oilfields and the global market. Ship-to-ship transfers have become a lifeline for Gulf producers as they adapt to the disruptions caused by the Iran war , which has entered its seventh month. Once loaded, a tanker disconnects and heads for its destination, typically a refinery in Asia. The "mother vessel" then returns to the Gulf via Hormuz to reload and repeat the process. The system cuts the distance any one ship must travel, reducing the risk of transiting the strait, even as an increasing number of tankers are crossing through a narrow corridor along Oman's coastline under US naval protection, with their navigation systems switched off. Exports through Hormuz have reached around 6.5 million barrels per day so far in September, the highest since the brief spike after the June ceasefire, according to Kpler data. This operation is a testament to the energy industry's ability to adapt to supply shocks. Yet, it is also a sign of how costly and complex it has become to move oil out of the world's most important exporting region. More on this [USN:L6N45A0SP TEXT:"in my latest column"]. The two conflicts that have dominated global energy markets are settling into a grim and costly stalemate, with neither showing any sign of a breakthrough. In other news: Trump's Achilles heel: My colleague Jamie McGeever and I looked at how surging diesel prices across the world, and in the US in particular, have become [USN:L6N4590YX TEXT:"a headache"] for President Donald Trump as the November midterm elections approach. Jet fuel crunch: Europe faces a fourth-quarter [USN:L6N4570XK TEXT:"jet fuel deficit"], even as it turns to far-flung suppliers including South Korea, which is set to boost its jet exports to Europe to a four-year high in September. Qatar's hobbled output: The crisis over the Strait of Hormuz [USN:S8N43E019 TEXT:"could delay"] some QatarEnergy expansion projects because critical equipment is unable to reach Qatar, its CEO Saad al-Kaabi said on Sunday, adding that QatarEnergy was producing only a "very minute" volume of liquefied natural gas. Back in Venezuela: Interim President Delcy Rodriguez on Saturday [USN:L1N45B050 TEXT:"signed"] a memorandum of understanding with TotalEnergies that will allow the French oil and gas company to return to the country years after it was forced out.
